INTEREST-RATE SCENARIOS

Define a shock. Revalue every cash flow.

Shift the whole zero curve or set a different shock at each tenor. Choose discounting, projection or both, then select scenarios in Data & valuation before running.

Shock convention: additive continuously compounded zero rates, ACT/365F tenors from each position’s settlement. Base curve coverage is unchanged; no rate floor is imposed. Bond cash flows remain contractual; mortgage prepayment equations are reevaluated; future floating resets and mortgage instalments are recalculated. Up to 10 scenarios. Definitions remain in this browser session; export to keep a record.

EXPLICIT ASSUMPTIONS

Know what drives value.

One EUR portfolio

Fixed, floating and zero-coupon bonds plus fixed and floating mortgages are valued from the lender / asset perspective. Product terms are separate from the workflow: enter data, review the balance sheet, run, then validate. Positions live in this browser session; download current inputs before leaving.

This is the first stage of a balance-sheet engine. Liability signs, net balance-sheet aggregation and regulatory interest-rate-risk measures are not yet modeled.

Reference rates and resets

A known current fixing plus the contractual spread applies until the next reset. At future resets, the full index tenor determines the forward rate. Monthly payments can reset quarterly; resets must align to payment boundaries and be no more frequent than payments.

Forward = (DFproj(start) / DFproj(end) − 1) / index accrual

Choose a named index with an index-matched curve, or explicitly use curve-implied mode. The ECB AAA curve is a sovereign reference, never relabelled as EURIBOR. Index tenor and reset interval are distinct; projection coverage may need to extend beyond final payment.

Mortgage amortization

Choose annuity, linear or interest-only. Fixed mortgages reconstruct scheduled balances from original principal. Floating mortgages after origination require current outstanding principal; seasoned annuities also require the current contractual instalment. Future resets recalculate annuity payments using remaining balance and maturity. Linear floating loans amortize current outstanding equally over remaining payments.

Mortgage interest = opening balance × annual rate / payments per year. Accrued interest is prorated by elapsed days in the current period. Negative floating coupons are allowed; no floor is assumed. Negative amortization is rejected.

Valuation and validation

Future cash flows are discounted using DF(payment) / DF(settlement). A mortgage discount spread is an additional explicit assumption; it differs from the contractual spread added to the reference rate. Payments on settlement are excluded. Mortgage prices per 100 use outstanding principal.

Product validation workbooks contain Excel formulas for forward rates, interest, totals, PV and principal / balance reconciliation. PASS means internal arithmetic reconciliation within EUR 0.01, not independent market-price validation. Recalculate in Excel after changing inputs; the export is an audit of this run, not a replacement amortization engine.

Mortgage prepayment

Select no prepayment, a constant annual CPR, or an equation returning annual CPR in percentage points (6 = 6%). Example: min(20, base_cpr_pct + 0.1 * age_months). For rate incentive: min(40, max(0, base_cpr_pct + 2 * (coupon_pct - market_rate_pct))).

Variables: base_cpr_pct, age_months, remaining_months, balance, original_principal, coupon_pct, market_rate_pct, period. Age and remaining months are measured at payment using ACT/365.25 × 12; period counts payment periods from origination. Balance is before scheduled principal. Market rate is the continuously compounded discount zero rate from settlement to payment, excluding the mortgage discount spread. Arithmetic, parentheses, ^ or ** powers and min/max/abs/exp/log/sqrt are supported. CPR must be finite and between 0 and 100; invalid equations produce a product error.

Prepayment follows scheduled principal at payment dates: remaining balance × [1 − (1 − CPR)^(1/frequency)]. The first partial period uses only the remaining fraction of that regular period. No historical prepayment is reconstructed. Annuity payments and linear principal reduce after prepayment; floating annuities still recast at rate resets. Contractual maturity stays unchanged unless CPR = 100% repays the loan sooner. No additional prepayment is applied at final maturity. Interest and accrued interest for the current period are calculated before prepayment. Equations are recalculated in each interest-rate scenario, so rate-sensitive prepayment can change fixed mortgage cash flows.

Equations and inputs remain in this browser session; download inputs to retain them. Model-document uploads and AI model generation are a future extension.

Model boundaries

No arrears, credit losses, caps/floors, fees, overnight compounding, reset lag or business-day adjustment. Mortgage periods must be regular and terms at most 50 years. Floating mortgage history is not reconstructed from today’s curve. Hybrid fixed-then-floating mortgages and resets inside a payment period require further development.
